text_blocks.snippet: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) were created by computer scientist Ian Goodfellow and his colleagues in June 2014.

Goodfellow coined the term and popularized the framework in a foundational 2014 paper co-authored with Yoshua Bengio and other researchers. The core design pits two neural networks against each other—a generator that creates fake data and a discriminator that tries to spot the fakes—in a zero-sum game. (Note: Some core adversarial concepts in neural networks were also explored earlier in the 1990s by Jürgen Schmidhuber, though Goodfellow established the modern GAN architecture).
